title: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
summary: Alice and Bob have an undirected graph with n nodes and three types of bidirectional edges: Type 1 can be traversed by Alice only, Type 2 by Bob only, and Type 3 by both.
statement: Alice and Bob have an undirected graph with n nodes and three types of bidirectional edges: Type 1 can be traversed by Alice only, Type 2 by Bob only, and Type 3 by both. Given an array of edges where each edge is represented as [type, u, v] for a bidirectional edge of type type between nodes u and v, find the maximum number of edges that can be removed such that the graph remains fully traversable by both Alice and Bob. The graph is fully traversable if starting from any node, both Alice and Bob can reach all other nodes. Return the count of removable edges, or -1 if full traversal is impossible.
constraints: Type one edges serve Alice, type two serve Bob, and type three serve both; nodes are one-based.
Remove as many edges as possible while both users can traverse the entire graph, or return -1.
hints: Use separate disjoint-set structures for Alice and Bob.
Process shared edges first, unioning both graphs but counting one physical edge when it joins components.
Then add useful private edges to their respective graph.
A spanning structure uses the minimum useful edges; everything else is removable, and disconnected final DSUs make the task impossible.
editorial: A spanning structure uses the minimum useful edges; everything else is removable, and disconnected final DSUs make the task impossible.

tests.explanation: Four edges suffice for both users, so two of the six can be removed.
Neither user can connect all four nodes, so the answer is negative one.
